title: startplasma-wayland overwrites $XKB_DEFAULT_*
line: Keyboard layout variables the user sets in .profile are no longer replaced by the system default when Plasma Wayland starts.
explanation: On Wayland, startplasma asks systemd-localed for the system keyboard model, layout, variant and options and exports them as XKB_DEFAULT_*. It did this unconditionally, so values the user had already exported before the session started (for example in .profile) were replaced by the system-wide defaults. The change only sets each XKB_DEFAULT_* variable from localed when it is not already set, as Nate suggested on the bug.

commits.message:
startplasma: don't overwrite XKB_DEFAULT_* variables that are already set

On Wayland, startplasma exported the keyboard settings from localed as
XKB_DEFAULT_* even when the user had already set them, e.g. in .profile,
so the system default won. Only set each variable when it isn't set yet.

BUG: 447203

media.caption: Session started with XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT=de and VARIANT=colemak: inside Plasma they are localed's us/dvorak
Same start with the fix: de/colemak are kept; MODEL (not set by the user) still comes from localed

review.text: Minimal, clean fix in `startplasma.cpp` that follows the maintainer guidance on the bug and prevents `systemd-localed` defaults from clobbering user-supplied `XKB_DEFAULT_*` variables. Using `qEnvironmentVariableIsSet(var)` is better than checking emptiness because it also respects intentionally empty overrides while still populating unset variables from `localed`. Before/after screenshots and normal-login verification confirm the fix without regressions.

reviews.text: Minimal, clean fix in `startplasma.cpp` that follows the maintainer guidance on the bug and prevents `systemd-localed` defaults from clobbering user-supplied `XKB_DEFAULT_*` variables. Using `qEnvironmentVariableIsSet(var)` is better than checking emptiness because it also respects intentionally empty overrides while still populating unset variables from `localed`. Before/after screenshots and normal-login verification confirm the fix without regressions.

The fix is in the right place (startplasma's localed import), small, and does what Nate sketched; the evidence shows de/colemak surviving when both LAYOUT and VARIANT are preset. But the check is per variable, and XKB layout, variant and options are coupled lists. In the reporter's exact steps (only XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT exported), a system with a localed variant or options still has them added, giving a mixed keymap such as favorite_layout(dvorak) that is not what the user asked for and may not compile. The rig never tested that case: it preset both variables, so the one-variable case the report describes is unverified.
changes: Treat the user's XKB settings as a whole: if any XKB_DEFAULT_* variable (or at least LAYOUT or VARIANT) is already set, skip importing layout/variant/options from localed, so they never get mixed with the system's (only MODEL may reasonably still come from localed).
Re-test with only XKB_DEFAULT_LAYOUT preset while localed has a non-empty variant, and update the commit message to describe the chosen rule.
